messages:
alex: Heads-up — merged terraform module bump for gpufleet from 1.2.3 -> 2.0.0 (PR: https://git.redwood/infra/+/4321). The change renames provider inputs and switches KMS key structure. gitops `plan` CI is now failing in eu-west1 due to provider alias conflicts + `az` quota errors.

priya: ACK. Saw the pipeline. It fails in the tf plan job with: 'Provider configuration for provider.aws is required but no configuration found.' also a bunch of diffs for kms_key_id -> kms_key_arn. :thinking:

sam: repro steps: checkout main, run `make tf-plan -C infra/gpufleet module=gpufleet` -> repros locally. CI output:
```
Error: Provider configuration not present
  on modules/gpufleet/main.tf line 12, in provider "aws":
 12: provider "aws" {}
```
Looks like the module now expects an aliased provider or different provider version.

mike: This is a semver-major change so not surprising. Two quick options: add a compatibility shim layer in the module that accepts both old var names and new ones, or revert the merge and open a v2-only module path (eg modules/gpufleet/v2). Shim is faster short-term.

jess: Also flag: eu-west1 has limited p4/8 capacity for our regions test account. The new default pool size in v2 bumped the default_node_count -> CI is trying to create a 32-GPU pool which trips quota/cost guardrails in staging. We should avoid a default change that scales up existing stacks.

alex: Good call. I missed the default bump PR note. For immediate unblock I'm going to: 1) revert the default_node_count in module inputs to previous value via a patch; 2) add a shim mapping for kms_key_id -> kms_key_arn; 3) pin provider requirement in module to aws ~> 4.40 in the root module. Will push shortly.

infra-ci: Pipeline failed: infra/gpufleet - terraform plan (gitops) — exit 1. See job 6842.

priya: For the shim, something like: 
```
variable "kms_key_id" { type = string; default = "" }
variable "kms_key_arn" { type = string; default = "" }
locals { kms_arn = var.kms_key_arn != "" ? var.kms_key_arn : length(var.kms_key_id) > 0 ? "arn:aws:kms:${data.aws_region.current.name}:${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:key/${var.kms_key_id}" : "" }
```
That avoids forcing users to change immediately.

sam: Also add a provider alias fallback block: if var.use_legacy_provider then use provider "aws" {}, else use provider "aws" { alias = "v2" } and pass providers = { aws = provider.aws, aws.v2 = provider.aws.v2 } to resources that need it. Ugly but effective for migration.

mike: Long term we should: publish modules/gpufleet/v2, tag module registry with migration notes, and add a tflint/tfsec acceptance test that runs a plan with existing state. Add a migration doc that includes `terraform state mv` or `import` steps for kms keys if names changed.

jess: I'm going to open a short runbook for staging ops: how to reduce requested gpu_count, how to force provider alias in environment for the region, and the billing owner to approve temporary quota bump. Will link.

alex: PR 4330: hotfix patch with shim + default rollback pushed. Also updated module README to document providers.lock requirement and added a note to CHANGELOG. Asking infra owners to approve quick patch release.

deploy-bot: deploy status: patch release gpufleet v1.2.4 published to internal registry. CD pipeline queued for staging.

priya: After patch merges we should add a CI gate: acceptance test that runs `terraform plan -var 'gpu_count=1'` against a mock account (no real creates) to catch default-bump regressions. Also add provider-version lockfile to repo.

sam: +1. I'll add a GH Actions job that does a dry-plan and checks for provider diff. Also will add note to dev-ex docs for module authors: never change defaults that affect infra size in a major bump without migration step.

mike: Side note: consider adding a sentinel check in gitops pipeline to prevent merges that change module defaults > 2x current values. Could be a cheap safety.

jess: Filing task for quota request for eu-west1 on behalf of test account. Link: https://console.aws/servicelimits/requests/submit?ticket=...

alex: Thanks everyone. Next actions: sam to add dry-plan CI job, priya to review shim code, jess to handle quota request, mike to draft migration plan for v2 path. I'll watch the staging plan and confirm rollback. :thumbsup:
